scope: All SQLite schema-plan model result.json files directly under jobs/<campaign>/<trial> available at audit time; counted denominator follows the two recorded campaign summaries. Control runs and rewritten/replayed scores are not included.

nul_contract.reason: All strings are literal default values; no NUL exclusion is specified. SQLite supports embedded NUL in TEXT and a constant expression can construct the value without embedding a raw NUL byte in SQL source.
nul_contract.sql_example: CREATE TABLE t(v DEFAULT(CAST(X'610062' AS TEXT))); INSERT INTO t DEFAULT VALUES; SELECT hex(v), typeof(v) FROM t;

raw_NUL_in_SQL_error.message: the query contains a null character

nul_contract.supersedes: Earlier working interpretation that this NUL test was a benchmark/spec mismatch was incorrect. Reference implementation choices do not define the public contract.

official_sources.support: SQLite permits embedded NUL in stored strings; display/quote/length behavior can obscure their contents.
The DEFAULT clause permits a constant expression enclosed in parentheses.

ambiguous_extra_assertions.note: The text requires decimal numeric strings but gives an ASCII qualifier only for identifier matching. The test requires rejection of fullwidth digits. This separate assertion needs contract interpretation; the reference parser is not itself the specification.

The test requires rejection of a digit separator accepted by some Python numeric parsers. Whether decimal numeric strings exclude separators should be assessed from the contract, not inferred from the reference implementation.

The test rejects drop=[v] with column_order=[v]. The instruction says to put surviving named columns first while also rejecting conflicting drops and changes. This is a separate ambiguity; no assertion is reclassified here.

clear_other_failure_example.observed: types={v: []} leaks TypeError: unhashable type: list
clear_other_failure_example.contract: instruction.md lines15 and32 require rejection of invalid option types through TransformError
